_comment: The questions a skeptical reader of a county's renewables profile asks, from Hawthorn's internal reviews of the
staff-only renewables pilot (2026-11-17 and 2026-11-19). The client-view-reviewer agent reads every profile
against them each day (docs/VERIFICATION_ROUTINE.md, section 5), and scripts/client_view_audit.py checks the
ones it can mechanically. Add a question here when a reader asks one the list does not cover; keep each one
generic (no client, no county) and say which check, if any, answers it.

questions.ask: Does the headline match the rules listed below it? A county with a moratorium or ban in force must not read as having no restrictions, and a ban or moratorium on another use (data centers) must not read as one on renewables.
How long has the moratorium been in force, and when does it end?
Has it been extended, and how many times?
Its end date has passed. Was it extended, replaced by an ordinance, or did it lapse?
Is the government drafting the ordinance the pause is waiting for?
Is this an outright ban, or a temporary pause? An ordinance that works as a ban weighs more than a true pause.
Is the record score, the core of the product, the first thing the page shows, with what feeds it below?
Where does the county rank nationally, not only in its state? Is it really among the most restrictive in the country?
Does the score count opposition organizing: a named group, a petition, a referendum drive, a lawsuit?
Do state siting board rules or a state law apply here, and does the page show them next to the local rules?
Is a court case pending that could void these local rules (for example, a county without zoning adopting a siting ordinance)?
What does the small model figure (the resemblance score) mean, and could a reader mistake it for the record score?
Can a reader see the weights behind the score, with the date they were set?
Are the weights set by hand or learned from outcomes, and what would it take to learn them?
Is every unverified or not-yet-checked rule labeled as such?
